bib.title: GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded

question: Can large multimodal models like GPT-4V act as generalist web agents that follow natural language instructions to complete tasks on any website, and what limits them?
hypothesis: LMMs can understand rendered webpages visually and plan well; the bottleneck is grounding the textual plan to the right HTML element, and the HTML-to-visual correspondence is the best lever.
contributions: SeeAct, a generalist web agent using LMMs for integrated visual understanding and acting
Three element-grounding strategies (attributes, textual choices, image annotation) plus oracle grounding
Multimodal Mind2Web, with screenshots aligned to HTML
An online evaluation tool (Playwright) for live websites
Offline and online evaluation and analysis, including SFT vs ICL and LMM vs LLM

method.summary: SeeAct prompts an LMM with a screenshot, task and previous actions to write a textual action description (action generation), then grounds it to an HTML element (e), operation (o) and value (v) by one of three methods. It is evaluated offline on Multimodal Mind2Web and online on 90 live-site tasks with a human monitor.

datasets.name: Multimodal Mind2Web (cleaned Mind2Web)
datasets.size: Test splits: Cross-Task 177 tasks, Cross-Website 142, Cross-Domain 694 (Table 1 rows as extracted: Train 1,009; Cross-Domain 694; Cross-Task 177; Cross-Website 142); Mind2Web has over 2,000 tasks over 137 websites, 31 low-level and 12 high-level domains
datasets.split: Cross-Task, Cross-Website, Cross-Domain; Train used only for SFT baselines
datasets.source: Mind2Web (Deng et al., 2023) with screenshots from the raw dump, human-verified for element visibility and rendering; released on HuggingFace osunlp/Multimodal-Mind2Web
datasets.preprocessing: HTML aligned with screenshots; ranker picks top 50 elements

datasets.name: Online subset
datasets.source: Mind2Web tasks run on live sites
datasets.preprocessing: Time-sensitive tasks rewritten (e.g. flight dates); tasks invalidated by website change resampled from the same split; non-login tasks only

models.name: Gemini Pro Vision
models.architecture: LMM, API; single-turn only so two turns merged

models.name: FLAN-T5-XL (MindAct)
models.init_from: fine-tuned on Mind2Web train with left-to-right LM objective

models.name: BLIP-2-T5-XL
models.architecture: CLIP ViT-L/14 encoder (frozen, image resolution 2,048) + bridge + FLAN-T5
models.init_from: FLAN-T5 initialised from Mind2Web fine-tuned weights; LLM and bridge fine-tuned jointly

models.name: GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 and GPT-4-turbo-1106-preview
models.architecture: text-only LLM, 3-shot ICL, MindAct multi-choice format

inference.samples: inferred: one run per task; no seeds or repeats reported
inference.prompting: Two-turn: (1) action generation prompt with system role, task, previous actions, screenshot, step-by-step analysis; (2) grounding prompt per method (Tables 7-9). Action generation uses screenshot only, no HTML. Action history in oracle online runs is produced by the model, summarised as Element/Operation/Value in another turn.
inference.retrieval: DeBERTa-base ranker top 50 elements; SeeAct clusters into groups of 17 options (online: three option groups); MindAct clusters into groups of 5 with iterative refinement

parameters.grounding_methods: attributes (element text and type, heuristic DOM search, model picks if several matches), textual choices, image annotation (red bounding boxes with bottom-left number labels, Supervision library)
parameters.online_extra_actions: PRESS ENTER and TERMINATE enabled for SeeAct-Choice

other.pop_ups: pop-up ads closed manually during online tests
other.oracle: humans identify the model's intended element/operation; online they perform the intended action
other.gemini_llava: best grounding method (choices) used for Gemini Pro Vision and LLaVA-1.5

metrics.name: Element Accuracy (Ele. Acc)
metrics.definition: predicted element compared with ground-truth elements

metrics.name: Operation F1 (Op. F1)
metrics.definition: token-level F1 of predicted operation (action and input value)

metrics.name: Step Success Rate (Step SR)
metrics.definition: step succeeds only if element and operation are both correct; macro average across tasks

metrics.name: Success Rate (SR)
metrics.definition: task succeeds only if all steps succeed; offline Offline0 no wrong step, Offline1 one wrong step allowed; online judged by human

eval.protocol: Offline on cached Mind2Web splits (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, oracle rows on 30-task-per-split subsets); online with Playwright tool, human monitors every step and judges success; no seeds, intervals or significance tests reported

prompts.purpose: Action generation system role and prompt (Table 6)
prompts.text: Imagine that you are imitating humans doing web navigation for a task step by step. At each stage, you can see the webpage like humans by a screenshot and know the previous actions before the current step decided by yourself through recorded history. You need to decide on the first following action to take. You can click an element with the mouse, select an option, or type text with the keyboard. ... You are asked to complete the following task: {TASK} Previous Actions: {PREVIOUS ACTIONS} (full text and the grounding prompts in Tables 7-9)

evidence.where: Table 1 text extraction flattens columns; row order Train, Cross-Domain, Cross-Task, Cross-Website with tasks 1,009/694/177/142 as printed

results.claim: GPT-4V with oracle (human) grounding completes 51.1% of tasks on live websites
results.setup: Online evaluation, 90-task subset of Multimodal Mind2Web (30 per test split), live websites, non-login tasks, GPT-4V (gpt-4-vision-preview), human monitors and judges each task; oracle grounding means human annotators execute the model's intended action
results.note: Conclusion rounds it to 'a success rate of 50%'.
results.quote:
Using oracle grounding further improves the performance substantially, reaching
a remarkable whole task success rate of 51.1%.

results.claim: SeeAct with real textual-choice grounding completes 37.8% of live-site tasks
results.setup: Online evaluation, 90-task subset of Multimodal Mind2Web (30 per test split), live websites, non-login tasks, GPT-4V (gpt-4-vision-preview), human monitors and judges each task; ranker top-50 candidates, groups of 17 options

Online evaluation, 90-task subset of Multimodal Mind2Web (30 per test split), live websites, non-login tasks, GPT-4V (gpt-4-vision-preview), human monitors and judges each task; MindAct two-stage setup, GPT-4 3-shot; FLAN-T5-XL fine-tuned on Mind2Web (8.9)

results.claim: Offline whole-task success (no error tolerance) is far below online: SeeAct-Choice 3.3 offline vs 37.8 online
results.setup: Same 90-task subset, Offline0 = no wrong step allowed; Offline1 allows one wrong step (12.2 for SeeAct-Choice)
results.note: Authors attribute gap to multiple viable plans per task; reference trace holds only one.

results.claim: Best real grounding leaves a 20-30% step-level gap to oracle grounding
results.setup: Step success rate, GPT-4V, 30 tasks per split; Table 3 gap Cross-Task 61.9 vs 39.1, Cross-Website 65.0 vs 32.7, Cross-Domain 62.1 vs 42.0
results.note: Intro says 20-30%, conclusion says 20-25%. On the online whole-task metric the gap is 51.1 - 37.8 = 13.3 points (computed).
results.quote:
The best
grounding strategy still has a 20-30% gap with oracle
grounding.

results.claim: Image-annotation grounding scores 20.3% step SR vs 39.1% for textual choices (Cross-Task)
results.setup: GPT-4V, 30-task subset per split, Cross-Task; Choices 39.1, Attributes 16.1, Oracle 61.9

results.claim: Cross-Website step SR: annotation 13.9 vs choice 32.7 vs attribute 12.1; Cross-Domain annotation 23.7 vs choice 42.0
54% of sampled image-annotation grounding errors are visual hallucination (made-up box/label); 46% are failures to link a box to its label
results.setup: 100 random action predictions with correct action generation but wrong grounding, image-annotation grounding, GPT-4V
results.quote:
Our analysis reveals that 54% of the errors can be attributed
to GPT-4V’s tendency of visual illusion

results.claim: Oracle-grounded GPT-4V step SR 61.9/65.0/62.1 across Cross-Task/Website/Domain
results.setup: Offline, 30 tasks per split, human-annotated oracle grounding
results.quote:
the
model achieves a step success rate of 61.9%, 65.0%, and
62.1% across three test splits, respectively.

results.claim: SeeAct-Choice with GPT-4V beats text-only GPT-4 in step SR by 6.8, 5.7 and 12.3 points across the three splits
results.setup: Offline; GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 evaluated on a 30-task-per-split subset (starred in Table 2); GPT-4V Table 2 row is full split
results.note: Table 2 GPT-4V Cross-Task Step SR 40.2 vs Table 3 SeeAct-Choice 39.1: full split vs 30-task subset.

results.claim: Oracle grounding leads second-best by 8.4% (Cross-Task), 23.9% (Cross-Website), 23.2% (Cross-Domain) step SR
results.setup: Offline, SeeAct-Oracle vs second-best method in Table 2
results.quote:
it achieves a 8.4% step success rate improvement over the
second-best method in the Cross-Task setting.

results.claim: Fine-tuned FLAN-T5-XL step SR in Table 2: 53.5 / 41.1 / 38.9; GPT-4V SeeAct-Choice 40.2 / 32.4 / 36.8
results.setup: Offline, Cross-Task; GPT-4V with Choices grounding, full test split
results.note: SFT beats SeeAct-Choice on Cross-Task step SR (53.5 vs 40.2); SeeAct is competitive, not better, with real grounding.
results.table: Table 2, row SEEACT - GPT-4V, column Cross-Task Step SR

results.claim: Gemini Pro Vision and LLaVA-1.5 with SeeAct-Choice reach 19.6 and 8.1 Cross-Task step SR, far below GPT-4V
results.table: Table 2, row SEEACT - GEMINI PRO VISION, column Cross-Task Step SR (LLaVA-1.5 8.1)

results.claim: Success falls with task length; the gap between Oracle and Choice widens on longer tasks (no single number; see Fig 3)
results.setup: Online, 90 tasks: Easy 1-4 actions (37 tasks), Medium 5-9 (35), Hard 10-18 (18); values read from Fig 3 only

results.claim: One screenshot of Figure 1 holds 423 HTML elements = 186,490 GPT-2 tokens vs 1,445 GPT-4V visual tokens
results.setup: Single example page (Figure 1), not an average
results.quote:
the
screenshot in Figure 1 contains 423 HTML elements that would
require 186,490 textual tokens with the GPT-2 Tokenizer,
while requiring only 1,445 visual tokens using GPT-4V’s
visual tokenizer.

limits: Headline 51.1% is with human oracle grounding, not an automatic agent; the best automatic grounding reaches 37.8% online
Online evaluation is 90 tasks, one run, human-judged, non-login tasks only, with manual pop-up closing and safety monitoring
GPT-3.5/GPT-4/oracle offline rows use 30-task-per-split subsets, so not directly comparable to full-split rows
Offline whole-task SR is stringent and underestimates because only one reference plan exists
SFT FLAN-T5-XL still beats SeeAct-Choice on offline Cross-Task step SR (53.5 vs 40.2)
Image-annotation grounding is weak in this paper (hallucinated labels); later models and mark methods may differ (dated: GPT-4V, Gemini Pro Vision, Jan 2024)
Textual choices struggle with identical elements; the model picks the first
No seeds, variance or significance reported

terms.definition: human annotators identify the model's intended actions, approximating a method that identifies (e, o, v) whenever mentioned in the action description

lineage.note: Dataset and MindAct two-stage ranker; generalist web agent definition
textual-choice grounding and ranker taken from it
image annotation effective on object-centric images but not on webpage screenshots here
